order: Archery fell short of those targets, failing for the first time in history to win a gold in the women's recurve event and finishing with three golds overall. Swimming was limited to one gold — three fewer than targeted — as Kim Woo-min, who had won three titles at the previous Games, was hampered by injury. Shooting and taekwondo each claimed three golds, while badminton took two.

Bright spots included basketball, which surpassed expectations by producing three golds — men's and women's 5-on-5 and men's 3-on-3. Baseball extended its winning streak to five consecutive Asian Games titles, and the men's football team claimed a fourth straight gold. Women's handball reclaimed the top spot for the first time in eight years, and team sports as a whole outperformed South Korea's showing at the Hangzhou Games.

China's swimming team alone produced 30 golds, spearheaded by Zhang Zhanshuo, who became the first swimmer in Asian Games history to win seven individual titles at a single edition. Athletics added 17 golds, shooting 16, wushu 12 and diving 10.

Kim Taek-soo, director of the national team training center, reflected on the results at a closing press conference Sunday. "Despite the disadvantages brought by changes in the sport structure, there were meaningful achievements — a diversification of medal-winning disciplines and first-ever golds in new sports," he said.

That standing began to erode at the 2018 Jakarta-Palembang Games, when the gold count dropped sharply to 49 and Korea slipped to third behind China and Japan. The downward trend continued through the 2022 Hangzhou Games (42 golds, 59 silvers, 89 bronzes) and into the current edition, with a third-place finish appearing to become the new norm.
Gold-medal hopes in athletics, sepak takraw, wushu and jiu-jitsu also went unfulfilled, contributing to the overall assessment of a disappointing performance.

South Korea had won more than 50 golds at every Asian Games from the 1986 Seoul Games (93 golds, 55 silvers, 76 bronzes) through the 2014 Incheon Games (79 golds, 70 silvers, 79 bronzes), finishing second overall seven times across those eight editions and cementing its reputation as a leading sports nation.

Excluding the 2018 Jakarta-Palembang Games — when Japan sent its top athletes ahead of a home Olympics and won 75 golds — the country had not exceeded 70 golds in the past four decades. This time Japan added more than 30 golds to its tally compared with the Hangzhou Games, where it won 52, making the improvement all the more striking.
